A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same InfoSEM study. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching content across appendix renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original GRN inference experiments on four BEELINE cell datasets, including benchmark comparisons, bias analyses, and sensitivity experiments in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds SCENIC comparisons, embedding sensitivity results, runtime measurements, and further InfoSEM accuracy results.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same prior construction, adjacency decomposition, MAP estimates, and variational objectives. GO and scBERT embeddings are tested through the existing prior mechanism as sensitivity variants; no new training or inference component is introduced.

E1.justification: Both versions use hESC, hHEP, mDC, and mESC, with cell-type-specific and non-cell-type-specific targets and seen- versus unseen-gene evaluations. The additions vary embeddings and input sizes within this coverage; no additional biological population or inference task is identified.

E2.justification: SCENIC is added to Table 2 and the corresponding appendix accuracy comparisons, now Tables 4–6. It also participates in the new runtime comparison. Existing comparator methods remain; this is a limited expansion of the baseline set.

E3.justification: v2 adds runtime evaluation in seconds at three cell/gene configurations: (454, 844), (758, 844), and (758, 1291). Figure 4 also adds GO and scBERT embedding configurations. Existing split procedures, accuracy metrics, and recall threshold remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 4 extends the existing embedding sensitivity analysis with GO and scBERT, testing whether these alternative priors help. Appendix B adds runtime comparisons across input sizes. The bias, downsampling, noisy-target, and cell-count sensitivity analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten train-test splits with different random seeds and report standard errors of the mean. Added accuracy rows follow the existing convention; no new statistical test, repeated-run policy, or uncertainty estimation procedure is described.

E6.justification: Result coverage expands substantially: Tables 4–5 supply previously absent InfoSEM-B/BC scores for seen-gene evaluations, alongside new SCENIC scores, embedding outcomes, and computational-cost results. Existing numerical accuracy entries are retained. The added comparator changes some rankings: in Table 2, SCENIC achieves hHEP Hit@1% of 0.568, exceeding InfoSEM-BC's unchanged 0.550.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations 1–17, including both ELBO derivations in Appendix A, are unchanged. Figure 1's label and diagram adjustments do not introduce a revised mathematical argument.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about informative priors, supervised benchmark biases, and unseen-gene evaluation, including the stated 38.5% and 11.1% improvements.

C2.justification: Section 5.2 adds hypotheses explaining scBERT's lack of improvement: information loss from expression binning and limited complementary information beyond scRNA-seq. It also adds an interpretation of InfoSEM's runtime overhead. Existing explanations and applicability claims remain.

D1.justification: New Appendix B provides per-method runtimes and associated cell/gene counts, adding computational-cost information. The hyperparameter documentation and promise to release code and datasets on acceptance are unchanged. Hardware, timing procedures, and SCENIC implementation details are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds the Gene Ontology reference, Ashburner et al. (2000), and expands discussion of alternative embeddings, including the already-cited scBERT work. The broader positioning relative to supervised GRN inference and DeepSEM is unchanged.

P1.justification: Editing is localized to the expanded sensitivity discussion, new runtime passages and appendix, updated cross-references, and conference publication notice. The main narrative, section sequence, and most wording remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 4 is enlarged and rearranged into stacked panels with additional embedding bars. v2 adds the runtime table, expands accuracy tables, and relocates appendix displays. Figure 1 receives diagram corrections, while Figure 5 becomes a sharper vector display of the same analysis.

improvement.justification: The SCENIC comparisons and previously missing InfoSEM seen-gene scores make the evaluation more complete. Expanded embedding tests establish a useful failure case, and runtime measurements add practical cost information. These gains are limited by missing implementation and timing details for the additions. The core method, theory, and original accuracy evidence remain unchanged, supporting an incremental overall improvement.
